hey there is really limited integration of posthog into the application here are some insights from the post hog application on some things needed and we also need better product understanding with funnels and other stuff: Here's the full picture. The data confirms your suspicion – tracking is significantly broken. Here's what's happening and why:

---

🔍 What the data shows

Last 30 days:

- ~95 total pageviews across the entire site
- The homepage / dominates with 69 views – the editor /editor/ only has 11
- /pricing/ had 2 visits, /settings/ 2, /signin/ 2
- Only 3 $identify calls total – meaning virtually everyone using the app is anonymous and untracked

The most telling signal: On almost every single day, pageviews = unique users. That means each person appears to only visit one page per session – which is impossible if they're actually using the app.

---

🐛 The two root causes

1. SPA navigation isn't being tracked

PostHog's JavaScript SDK automatically captures pageview events on page load. The problem with single-page apps is that page loads don't happen beyond the initial one – meaning user navigation inside the app isn't tracked at all.

So when a user loads the homepage and then navigates to the editor, PostHog only sees the homepage visit. Every subsequent page they visit is invisible.

The fix: You can opt-in to tracking SPA navigation by setting the defaults config option to the most recent date when initializing PostHog. Recent defaults set capture_pageview: 'history_change', which captures SPA navigation using the browser history API.

For Next.js app router, the recommended approach is to use a PostHogProvider component initialized with updated defaults – see the SPA pageview tracking tutorial (https://posthog.com/tutorials/single-page-app-pageviews) for the exact setup.

2. Users aren't being identified after sign-in

Only 2 users were identified in the past 30 days. This means everyone who signs in and uses the editor is being tracked as an anonymous visitor with a random ID. When they come back the next day, PostHog sees them as a brand new person.

The fix: Call posthog.identify() after a user successfully signs in:

posthog.identify(user.id, {
 email: user.email,
 name: user.name,
})

This should happen in your auth callback / sign-in success handler. See the Next.js identify example (https://posthog.com/questions/next-js-app-directory-client-side-tracking-identify-example) for how to wire this up in the app router.

---

📋 What to fix first

Priority | Fix | Impact
🔴 High | Enable SPA pageview capture (capture_pageview: 'history_change') | Will immediately reveal real usage – editor visits, feature usage, navigation paths
🔴 High | Call posthog.identify() on sign-in | You'll start tracking returning users, sessions, and retention properly
🟡 Medium | Mark your own account as a test account | Filters your dev activity out of stats

Once these two fixes are in, you should see a dramatic jump in tracked events and you'll finally be able to answer questions like "how many Discord users came and actually used the editor?"

Then I’ll verify the current PostHog SPA guidance against the linked docs and implement the smallest coherent event model for funnels—not just pageviews.

content.text: The first browser run confirms the Twyne app itself hydrates cleanly, but this checkout intentionally has no local PostHog key, so zero analytics requests are expected. I’m starting a second local-only verification server with a fake public key and aborting every PostHog network request in the browser; that lets me prove the SDK emits initial and history-change events without polluting production.

I’m cleaning up the temporary browser interception and local servers, then doing the final diff/review pass.

The owner’s person property is correctly set to `$internal_or_test_user = true`, but the dynamic cohort last calculated earlier today and has not refreshed yet. I’m re-saving its unchanged filter definition solely to trigger PostHog’s documented cohort recalculation; I’m not changing the project-wide default filter setting.

The final diff review caught one subtle session-counting issue: switching away from a folio and back would re-arm its `first_edit` milestone, inflating activation. I’m tightening that now so each folio can emit `first_edit` only once per page session, while still resetting its word-count baseline on load.

content.text:
You’re right: the earlier work fixed behavioral analytics and funnels, but it did not build a closed-loop AI evaluation and user-feedback system.

| Area | Current state | Missing |
|---|---|---|
| PostHog AI observability | `$ai_generation` events are arriving | No automated evaluations, score definitions, review queues, provider, or trace-linked feedback |
| Surveys | None | Live PostHog project has zero surveys; application has no survey integration |
| Arize | Live `twyne` project and server tracing exist | Continuous evaluator/task status is unverified; installed `ax` client is incompatible with the current API response |
| Offline evals | Substantial repository harness exists | Results are disconnected from production traces, releases, and product outcomes |

Key technical problems:

- Server generations use the hard-coded identity `convex-server`, so AI quality cannot be joined to authenticated users, retention, folios, or survey responses: [convex/posthog.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/convex/posthog.ts:74).
- PostHog traces have no AI session ID, token counts, or cost information.
- “Eval signals” in [ai-evals.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/ai-evals.ts:39) are only event properties—not actual judges or scores.
- Client coverage is incomplete. The streamed interview path bypasses tracked generation capture: [ai-client.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/utils/ai-client.ts:2478). Direct audio transcription also bypasses it.
- Inputs and outputs can include up to 6,000 characters of manuscript content. That needs an explicit privacy/redaction policy before broadening evaluation access.
- The repository already has useful offline suites—grounding, helpfulness, rubric behavior, interviews, apparatus selection, and robustness—starting with [judge.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/evals/judge.ts:2) and the scripts in [package.json](/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/package.json:53). They are not connected to production monitoring.

The next integration should be:

1. Propagate authenticated distinct ID, anonymous ID, folio/session ID, and editorial-action ID through every generation.
2. Add deterministic checks for structured output, valid scoring ranges, protocol adherence, and citation/source integrity.
3. Backfill a small production sample with grounding/helpfulness judges, review the explanations, then enable sampled continuous evaluation.
4. Add contextual feedback immediately after AI output: thumbs up/down plus reason chips, linked to the exact trace.
5. Add a lightweight “Did this help you make progress?” survey after meaningful milestones such as dossier completion or export—not a generic early NPS interruption.
6. Build the real quality funnel:

`AI requested → generation succeeded → eval passed → user marked helpful → revision/export completed → user returned`

7. Route failed evaluations, negative feedback, and high-value error traces into a human review queue.

The live PostHog project currently shows zero evaluations, zero scores, zero queues, and zero surveys, so this remains genuinely unfinished. I made no additional changes during this audit.
